# From an index to a memory offset

[The point (1,1,1) can be the first element of an array. Its coordinates need not be its offset.]{.lesson-deck}
:::

A mathematical field has several indices; a contiguous C++ buffer has one.
Before writing an FFT, stencil or file, we need a precise map between
those descriptions. This refactors example 06 around a nonzero lower
corner, where an accidental assumption about the origin becomes visible.

## Subtract the lower corner first

For an inclusive box with lower corner $(\ell_x,\ell_y,\ell_z)$ and
sizes $(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, OpenPFC uses the x-fastest offset

$$
p(i,j,k)=(i-\ell_x)+n_x(j-\ell_y)+n_xn_y(k-\ell_z).
$$ {#eq-offset}

Our box runs from $(1,1,1)$ through $(2,2,2)$. It contains eight points,
not one: the size of an inclusive interval is $h-\ell+1$.
Equation @eq-offset sends $(1,1,1)$ to zero and $(2,1,2)$ to five.

## Let the box own the map

```{.cpp include="model.cpp" snippet="indexing" dedent=2}
```

The output is a small table of `i,j,k,offset,value`. The stored value is
the affine function $2i+j+3k$. This separates two concerns: `to_linear`
decides where the value belongs, and the lambda decides what it is.

The test reads the actual table and requires offsets `0,1,...,7` in
iteration order. The executable also checks the endpoint values and an
interior stride. We do not infer correct indexing merely because the
program stayed within the allocated buffer.

## A one-line experiment

```sh
openpfc run model.cpp input.json --launcher=none
```

This lesson has no numerical input parameters; change the box in
[model.cpp](model.cpp). First shift both corners by ten without changing
the box size. The offsets should remain zero through seven, while the
function values change. Then change only the upper x index to three,
resize the buffer and predict the new y and z strides.

The tempting mistake is to use `i + nx*j + nx*ny*k` for a box whose lower
corner is nonzero. That expression belongs to a zero-origin local array;
it does not implement @eq-offset for global indices.

## Padding changes the question

This example concerns a compact box. A halo-padded `Field` has extra
storage around the owned box. Use that field's own `idx` for its buffer,
and `Box3i::to_linear` for the compact box it describes. The
next lesson makes the difference concrete.
See the [Box3i header](https://github.com/ahojukka5/OpenPFC/blob/master/include/openpfc/kernel/data/box3i.hpp)
for the exact indexing contract.
The complete [C++ model](model.cpp) and [starting input](input.json)
are available with this lesson.
